channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Incêndios na Amazônia caíram a mínimo histórico em 2025
item.description: In 2025, Amazon wildfires fell to their lowest level since records began in 1985, with only 3.1 million hectares burned — a sharp decline from 15.8 million hectares in 2024, according to MapBiomas. The drop, attributed to delayed rains, reduced deforestation, and heightened community awareness following 2024’s devastating fires, was praised as a policy success for President Lula’s re-election bid in October 2026. However, fire levels in the Cerrado remained comparable to the previous year.

item.title: Com prazo curto, Flávio Bolsonaro corre contra o tempo para encontrar vice com potencial
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, the PL’s pre-candidate for president, is racing against time to find a female running mate after a public rift with Michelle Bolsonaro. He has approached Senator Tereza Cristina (PP), deputies Simone Marquetto and Clarissa Tércio, and economist Daniella Marques (Republicanos), but none have accepted, with allies acknowledging some candidates lack competitiveness. Both PP and Republicanos insist on neutrality, prioritizing congressional strength over presidential alignment.

item.title: Nordeste ganhou 1,1 milhão de eleitores em 4 anos; Sudeste perdeu
item.description: The Northeast gained 1.14 million voters between 2022 and 2026, reaching 43.53 million, while the Southeast lost 378,090 voters, driven by a decline in São Paulo. Despite the loss, the Southeast remains the largest electoral college with 66.33 million voters. The Northeast's growth benefits Lula (PT), a region historically favorable to the left, while the Southeast's decline hinders Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL) campaign, given his poor performance there in 2022.

item.title: Jogos de hoje, terça, 21 de julho: onde assistir futebol ao vivo e horários
item.description: On Tuesday, July 21, 2026, there are key matches in the Brasileirão Série A and B, along with Copa Sudamericana playoffs and the Supercopa Argentina. Highlights include Atlético Mineiro vs Bahia at 7:30 PM (Sportv and Premiere) and Universidad Central vs Santos at 9:30 PM (SBT, ESPN and Disney+), a decisive match for Santos' continuation in the continental tournament.

item.title: Governo deve se reunir com setores afetados por tarifaço dos EUA
item.description: The Brazilian government will meet with representatives from sectors most affected by the new 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian exports, effective July 22, which are expected to impact 18% of Brazil’s exports to the U.S. (US$7.4 billion in 2024). Discussions, led by the MDIC and Finance Ministry, include expanding the Brazil Sovereign Plan, financial aid, and market diversification, with exceptions for coffee, beef, fish, rare earths, and orange. Vice President Alckmin confirmed a support program for impacted sectors, mirroring the response to Trump’s 2025 tariff increase.

item.title: A reunião entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Marcos Pereira para tentar a aliança na disputa pela Presidência
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro of the PL and Marcos Pereira of the Republicans met on Thursday night with Rogério Marinho to attempt to form an alliance for the 2026 presidential race. The meeting was held in the evening and reported as exclusive content for subscribers, with no specific terms of the negotiation disclosed.

item.title: Kalil é eleito "novo Ciro Gomes" por ala do PDT
item.description: A faction of the PDT has begun referring to Alexandre Kalil, the pre-candidate for governor of Minas Gerais, as the 'new Ciro Gomes' due to his criticisms of President Lula and the PT, echoing Ciro Gomes' stance within the party. The nickname emerged after Kalil skipped the PDT's national convention in Brasília, where Lula was present, causing discontent among party leaders.

item.title: Bancada do Master sofre baixas nas eleições e tenta sobreviver em pré-campanha
item.description: The Banco Master scandal led to the withdrawal of Cláudio Castro (PL) and Ibaneis Rocha (MDB) from Senate candidacies following investigations and political fallout tied to banker Daniel Vorcaro. Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) also saw his polling drop after audio emerged showing he requested money from Vorcaro to fund a film about his father, ex-president Jair Bolsonaro. The so-called 'Bancada do Master' is attempting to survive in the pre-campaign phase amid mounting scrutiny over its ties to the businessman.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio cogitam apoiar Garotinho ao governo do RJ após novo revés em chapa do PL
item.description: Leaders of Rio de Janeiro's PL party are considering supporting Anthony Garotinho (Republicanos) for governor after Flávio Bolsonaro's ticket lost its running mate, Douglas Ruas, following Rogério Lisboa's withdrawal. Garotinho has officially launched his candidacy with Marcelo Crivella as his Senate pre-candidate, while the PL evaluates replacing Márcio Canella with Crivella due to Canella's arrest for illegal firearm possession. A potential PL-Republicans alliance aims to strengthen the right-wing position in the state.

item.title: Qual é a data das eleições de 2026 para presidente, governador, senador e deputado?
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections will take place in two rounds: the first round on October 4 for president, governor, senator, and deputies; the second round, if needed, on October 25. Electoral campaigning begins on August 16, and the deadline to regularize voter registration is May 6, 2026.

item.title: Charge do Aroeira
item.description: The Aroeira cartoon, published on Blog do Noblat, reflects the current Brazilian political landscape: Lula is smiling in the polls while the opposition is struggling, symbolized by 'bleeding'. The post also mentions state-level conventions solidifying candidacies and alliances, along with articles on diverse topics such as sports and international politics.

item.title: Valdemar quer Aécio na chapa do PL em Minas
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto negotiated a possible alliance with Aécio Neves' PSDB in Minas Gerais, proposing the tucano as a Senate candidate on the PL ticket. The PL has not yet decided whether to launch its own gubernatorial candidate or support Cleitinho (Republicanos), while Aécio has not given a definitive answer, also weighing offers from MDB and PDT. The PL hopes the Minas alliance will lead to PSDB support for Flávio Bolsonaro's presidential bid.

item.title: Lula pede a sindicalista críticas mais duras a presidente da Fiesp após tarifas dos EUA; veja vídeo
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva urged the CSB labor confederation to take a tougher stance against Fiesp president Paulo Skaf after the business group blamed the federal government for U.S. 25% tariffs on Brazilian exports. Lula made the request during the PDT convention that formalized his re-election support, speaking with CSB leader Antonio Neto on stage. He also challenged U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to openly back his rival Flávio Bolsonaro, declaring Brazil would defeat any foreign interference in its democracy.

item.title: Lula sinaliza um 4º governo de austeridade e freio no assistencialismo
item.description: Lula signals that, in a potential fourth term, he intends to adopt a fiscal austerity agenda, halting new inclusion policies and maintaining only existing social spending to balance accounts and perpetuate PT in power. Previously, Flávio Bolsonaro was seen as a strong candidate to defeat him, even praised by influential bankers for his appearance. The prospect of another Lula government causes insomnia in Faria Lima, which fears eight more years of high spending that scares away investors.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio planeja divulgar áudios entre Lulinha e empresária
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign is considering the early release of audio recordings between Lulinha, the eldest son of President Lula, and businesswoman Roberta Luchsinger, as a countermeasure amid political pressure. The material, originally planned for release in August, may be disclosed sooner to undermine the government's image.

item.title: Governo Lula aproveita reação ao tarifaço dos EUA para se aproximar do empresariado antes da eleição
item.description: The Lula government is seeking to reconnect with the business community amid backlash over U.S. tariffs, using the moment to strengthen its political base ahead of the 2026 elections. After tensions with productive sectors over issues like the 6x1 work schedule and the 'blusinhas' tax, the administration sees the Brazil Soberano plan as an opportunity for dialogue and alignment with the private sector, historically more aligned with right-wing candidates.

item.title: União-PP reforça afastamento de Flávio e deve confirmar neutralidade, mas Republicanos mantém negociação por aliança com PL
item.description: The União-PP federation is leaning toward neutrality in the 2026 presidential election, aligning with the stance being evaluated by Republicanos, despite Flávio Bolsonaro’s attempts to re-engage these parties. The leaders of the three parties did not attend the União-PP state convention in São Paulo due to local commitments, but Republicanos leaves the door open for negotiation, conditioning any support on the PL nominating a Republicanos vice-presidential candidate and backing Republicanos candidates in key states such as Mato Grosso and Roraima.

item.title: Flávio articula encontro reservado com Milei para reforçar ofensiva internacional antes da convenção do PL
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is arranging a private meeting with Argentine President Javier Milei in São Paulo, hours before the PL convention that will formalize his presidential candidacy. The meeting is part of a strategy to strengthen his international alignment with conservative leaders, following a prior meeting in Buenos Aires last month. Milei’s presence at the PL convention will be treated as a public demonstration of international support for Flávio’s candidacy.

item.title: PL oficializará candidatura de Flávio sem vice diante de impasse com Republicanos e disputa interna na legenda
item.description: The PL will officially nominate Flávio Bolsonaro as its presidential candidate without announcing a running mate, leaving the vice-presidential slot open until August 5 to allow for negotiations with the Republicanos and internal party resolution. Economist Daniella Marques, affiliated with Republicanos, is a leading contender for the vice-presidential spot, but her nomination hinges on progress in state-level alliances, which are currently limited to Espírito Santo. Internal PL resistance exists, with party president Valdemar Costa Neto doubting her electoral appeal.

item.title: 'Green card' para Eduardo Bolsonaro nos EUA teve 'habilidades extraordinárias' como justificativa, diz aliado
item.description: Allied journalist Paulo Figueiredo stated that Eduardo Bolsonaro’s U.S. Green Card was granted based on 'extraordinary abilities'. The permanent residency allows indefinite stay and work in the U.S., and Eduardo said he exiled himself due to persecution in Brazil, thanking the Trump administration. The move came amid U.S.-Brazil trade tensions, drawing criticism from the left, who labeled it a 'payment for betrayal'.

item.title: Anúncio do Republicanos amplia isolamento de Ruas no Rio, e Flávio atua junto à federação União-PP para conter crise
item.description: The PL in Rio faces increasing isolation in Douglas Ruas's pre-candidacy for Guanabara Palace, following Rogério Lisboa's (PP) withdrawal and the Republicans' announcement of Anthony Garotinho as their own candidate. Flávio Bolsonaro is seeking support from the União-PP federation to prevent neutrality that would favor Eduardo Paes (PSD), but encountered resistance, notably Antonio Rueda's (União Brasil) absence at a São Paulo event. Despite Flávio's national appeal, an alliance with the federation remains distant, according to Valdemar Costa Neto.

item.title: Excesso de cautela com defeso eleitoral gera apagão de dados públicos que compromete acesso à informação
item.description: The 2026 electoral blackout, in effect since July 4, has led public agencies to remove large volumes of data due to overly cautious interpretations of the ban on institutional publicity. Portals such as Ibama, Agência Brasil, Inpe, the National Archive, and Brasil Participativo became inaccessible, undermining scientific research and public policy formulation. Although the law only prohibits promoting government acts during the electoral period, restrictive enforcement has caused a temporary blackout of essential information.

item.title: Daniella diz que programa de celulares de Flávio foi mal interpretado
item.description: Daniella Marques, coordinator of Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign, said the proposal to expand internet and cellphone access for women and the elderly was misinterpreted, denying it involves indiscriminate distribution of devices. She clarified the initiative is still under study and would include data bonuses for Gov.br access and phone provision only for those unable to afford them, based on partnerships with telecom companies and subject to financial viability.

item.title: Cotada a vice de Flávio, Daniella diz que “mulheres não são vítimas”
item.description: Daniella Marques, a member of Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign economic team and former president of Caixa, defended the 'Brasil por Elas' program during a live stream with Eduardo Bolsonaro, asserting that women are not victims of society but strong and capable of achieving economic autonomy. She explained the program is based on social and economic indicators to promote digital inclusion, professional qualification, and labor market insertion, addressing the burden of unpaid care work, which accounts for 8.5% of Brazil’s GDP. Daniella argued that public policies should prioritize economic freedom, entrepreneurship, and security, rejecting victimization narratives and placing the feminist agenda at the core of the campaign.

item.title: Eduardo diz que PT terá dificuldade para ter nova liderança após Lula
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro claimed the PT would struggle to build a new national leadership if Lula loses in 2026, criticizing the left's lack of unity and promoting Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign as an alternative. During the live with Daniella Marques, he emphasized digital inclusion, professional qualification, and women's entrepreneurship, while attacking the Judiciary and Lula's government for alleged gender policy inconsistencies.

item.title: Nunes diz que Flávio vai resgatar a soberania nacional se for eleito
item.description: São Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes (MDB) stated that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president, will defend the 'recovery of national sovereignty' if elected, echoing a slogan used by the Lula administration. Speaking at the União Progressista federation convention in São Paulo, Nunes outlined Bolsonaro’s platform as including anti-corruption efforts, lowering the age of criminal responsibility, and family values. He urged center-right unity to avoid vote-splitting in São Paulo’s Senate race, endorsing federal deputy Guilherme Derrite (PP) and Alesp president André do Prado (PL).

item.title: Um presidente de mãos atadas governará o Brasil
item.description: The author draws a parallel between the inflated expectations surrounding the World Cup and the current electoral optimism, arguing that just as Brazil failed to win the hexa despite commercial hype, the next president will govern under significant institutional and political constraints, effectively having their hands tied. The piece warns against illusions of radical change in the 2026 elections, urging realism in light of Brazil’s entrenched power structures.

item.title: Lula testa discurso de campanha ao desafiar Rubio e sugere que EUA podem trabalhar pela candidatura de Flávio
item.description: President Lula tested a campaign speech challenging U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to openly support Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy, suggesting possible foreign interference in Brazil’s 2026 elections. He defended national sovereignty, accused Bolsonaro allies of treason for seeking international sanctions against Brazil, and emphasized Brazil’s right to self-determination. The event featured explicit PDT support, with Carlos Lupi framing Lula as an antidote to Trumpism.

item.title: Número de brasileiros que votam no exterior cresce 32% e chega a 919 mil; veja principais cidades
item.description: The number of Brazilians eligible to vote abroad grew by 31.8% between 2022 and 2026, reaching 918,9 thousand voters. Lisbon recorded the highest increase at 74.1%, while the United States remains the country with the largest contingent of Brazilian voters abroad. The growth also reflects voter registration updates, not solely immigration trends.

item.title: Preso, Bolsonaro se livra de caso da 'Abin paralela', mas ainda é investigado em outras frentes
item.description: Justice Alexandre de Moraes archived the 'parallel Abin' investigation involving Jair Bolsonaro, as the evidence had already been used in his conviction for attempting a coup d'état. However, Bolsonaro remains under investigation in the STF for fake news, digital militias, jewelry diversion, and incitement during the pandemic. His sons, including Carlos Bolsonaro, are also still subject to ongoing inquiries.

item.title: Decisão de Gonet tira da mira do STF senador que pediu indiciamento de ministros
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet has referred Minister Gilmar Mendes' request to investigate Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE) to Sergipe's Electoral Public Ministry, removing the case from the Supreme Court's (STF) jurisdiction. This decision produces two effects: it strips the STF of authority to review the request and shifts the investigation to the state level, where Vieira only has privileged jurisdiction for common crimes. The original request sought to indict Vieira for having called for the indictment of STF justices.

item.title: Democracia, privatizações, recado aos EUA: discurso de Lula em convenção do PDT indica tom de campanha à reeleição
item.description: Lula spoke at the PDT convention, reinforcing support for his re-election and defending democracy, national sovereignty, and social inclusion. He criticized Bolsonaro-era privatizations, calling members of the Bolsonaro family 'traitors of the Fatherland' and challenged U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to openly support Flávio Bolsonaro’s candidacy, saying 'let him come, let him form a committee'.

item.title: Flávio encontra aliados no Guarujá e discute propostas de campanha
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) met with allies in Guarujá to discuss campaign strategies and government priorities, emphasizing the fight against drug trafficking at the Port of Santos. He announced that, starting in 2027, any drug trafficker using the Port of Santos will be arrested or neutralized. The meeting also included a helicopter flyover of the Baixada Santista to record electoral propaganda material.

item.title: Tarcísio elogia Nunes e crítica Haddad: “Ministro do Paraguai”
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas praised Mayor Ricardo Nunes and indirectly criticized Fernando Haddad, calling him the 'worst finance minister' and comparing him to Paraguay's 'best finance minister'. He claimed São Paulo's success stems from the absence of left-wing governments and asserted the left will never govern the state.

item.title: “A direita do Ceará está vendida”, diz Michelle após fala de Ciro
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro criticized the right in Ceará for supporting Ciro Gomes (PSDB) over Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) for president, claiming the Ceará right is "sold" due to political deals. She highlighted a family rift with her stepson, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who backs Ciro, while she supports Eduardo Girão (Novo-CE). The tension arose after videos in which Michelle accused Flávio of disrespect and pressuring her to step aside from PL decisions.

item.title: Câmara envia atas a Dino e diz que emendas foram regulares
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies sent documents to Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino proving that the processing of parliamentary amendments followed internal regulations, emphasizing that budget execution is the Executive's responsibility. The Chamber attached meeting minutes, Sinec system records, and confirmed that indicated beneficiaries were the actual recipients, ruling out embezzlement. The response reaffirms commitment to transparency and traceability, aligned with the Joint Work Plan approved by the STF in ADPF 854.

item.title: Cotada à vice de Flávio Bolsonaro diz: "Mulher de direita não é submissa"
item.description: Daniella Marques, former president of Caixa Econômica Federal and a leading candidate for vice-president on Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket, rejected the notion that right-wing women are submissive, stating that men and women are equal before God and that families should have freedom to define their own roles. She acknowledged biological differences but rejected the idea that women must compete with men to be strong, emphasizing partnership in marriage and family. Her remarks come as negotiations between PL and Republicans remain stalled over support for candidates in Roraima and Mato Grosso, delaying her official nomination.

item.title: O dado surpreendente de pesquisa sobre eleição no DF com Michelle Bolsonaro no páreo
item.description: The Paraná Pesquisas survey reveals Michelle Bolsonaro trailing Leila Barros in the Senate race for the Federal District, surprising VEJA’s politics editor who expected her to lead. Governor Celina Leão heads the race for Palácio do Buriti, while Ibaneis Rocha’s withdrawal from the race reshaped the contest, opening opportunities for new candidates.

item.title: O fator que pode fazer o eleitor recorrer ao voto útil na eleição presidencial de 2026
item.description: The rise in undecided voters — those declaring blank, null votes or preferring candidates outside the polarization — may trigger a useful voting movement as early as the first round of the 2026 presidential election. According to political scientist Fábio Vasconcellos, this group grew from 24% in 2022 to 32% today, reflecting increasing aversion to the Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro dichotomy. Despite Lula having lower disapproval than Bolsonaro did in 2022, his lead has dropped from 17 to 8 points, showing that incumbent disadvantage has not translated into stronger competitiveness.

item.title: Lula desafia Marco Rubio a apoiar Flávio Bolsonaro: “Vamos derrotar todos”
item.description: At the PDT national convention in Brasília, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva challenged U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to publicly support his rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, in the 2026 elections, declaring he would 'defeat all' who interfere in Brazil’s democratic process. Lula accused Rubio and others of politically motivated pressure, citing new U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods as retaliation linked to electoral interference. The convention also formalized the PDT’s endorsement of Lula’s reelection bid.

item.title: Tarcísio elogia Bolsonaro: “O cara que rompeu paradigmas”
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) praised former President Jair Bolsonaro (PL) at a convention of the São Paulo branch of the União Brasil-PP federation, calling him "the man who broke paradigms". The event also confirmed Guilherme Derrite (PP-SP) as the Senate candidate for São Paulo. This marks the first joint appearance of Tarcísio and Bolsonaro at a political event since the 2022 elections.

item.title: ‘Vamos derrotar todos’, diz Lula sobre possível apoio de Rubio a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: President Lula (PT) stated that U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio might be supporting Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) by potentially 'setting up a committee' to aid him in the 2026 elections, vowing to defeat 'all' in defense of democracy. He emphasized that Brazil's internal politics must be decided by Brazilians without foreign interference, following Rubio’s criticisms of Lula over the U.S.-Brazil tariff dispute.

item.title: A grande diferença entre as eleições de 2022 e 2026 que é uma má notícia para Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The growing neutrality of the Centrão (Union Brazil, PP, Republicans) in the 2026 elections, contrasting with their explicit support in 2022, hinders Flávio Bolsonaro’s ability to build alliances, reflecting his failure to expand his political base and the fragmentation of center parties. This trend is seen as bad news for his candidacy, as it removes a potential pillar of support in the first round.

item.title: Sem direção nacional, União e PP de SP oficializam apoio a Flávio
item.description: São Paulo's PP and União Brasil parties officially endorsed Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) for president in a state convention today. However, the União Progressista federation is expected to remain neutral in the national race despite the state-level support. The move highlights internal divisions within the party alliance.

item.title: Brasil ganha 2,3 milhões de novos eleitores; saiba qual foi a única região que registrou queda
item.description: Brazil will have 158,745,463 eligible voters for the 2026 elections, an increase of 2.29 million compared to 2022, according to the TSE. The 1.46% growth in the voter registry was recorded across all regions except one, which experienced a decline — though the content does not specify which region. This expansion reflects the growing national electorate ahead of the presidential election.

item.title: Flávio cita convite de Ciro Nogueira e sinaliza aproximação
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro said he was invited by Ciro Nogueira to attend the União Progressista state convention in São Paulo, signaling openness to a national alliance between PL, PP and União Brasil, still under negotiation. He criticized the Lula government, stating Brazil cannot endure four more years of PT, and highlighted support from the UP’s São Paulo directory, despite the absence of Ciro Nogueira and Antônio Rueda at the event. Negotiations are ongoing, with Simone Marquetto a leading candidate for vice president, and the PP national convention deadline set for August 5.

item.title: Condenado no Brasil e premiado com green card nos EUA, qual a pátria de Eduardo Bolsonaro?
item.description: Eduardo Bolsonaro, former federal deputy and son of Jair Bolsonaro, obtained a U.S. green card after being convicted in Brazil to 4 years and 2 months in prison for coercion against the Supreme Federal Court, in an attempt to interfere in the case against his father over an alleged coup plot. Despite claiming to be a 'political exile', he lives in the U.S. with financial support from his father and works to advance American interests against Brazil, while thousands of Brazilians are deported by ICE. His situation reveals a clear loyalty to the U.S., not Brazil, where he is ineligible for eight years and has lost his position in the Federal Police.

item.title: Lula é “antídoto à desgraça chamada Trump”, diz Carlos Lupi
item.description: PDT national president Carlos Lupi stated that Donald Trump represents 'the disgrace of society' and that Lula is the 'antidote' to him, praising the former president as a patriot and defender of Brazil's left-wing historical legacy. Lupi endorsed the PT leadership's expectation that Lula could win in the first round of the 2026 elections, while Marília Arraes labeled Bolsonarism as destined for 'the trash can of history'. The PDT formally announced its support for Lula's re-election at its national convention in Brasília.

item.title: Sem citar nomes, Lula volta a insinuar que Flávio é traidor do Brasil
item.description: President Lula again implied that Flávio Bolsonaro is a traitor to Brazil, linking the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods to his activities in the United States. He repeated his claim that traitors were once hanged, echoing a June statement about the Bolsonaro clan. The remark contains a historical error, confusing the fate of Joaquim Silvério dos Reis with that of Tiradentes.

item.title: Lula: Se depender de mim, vamos ganhar as eleições no 1º turno
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) stated that, if it depends on him, he aims to win the 2026 presidential election in the first round. The comment was made during the PDT’s national convention in Brasília, reflecting growing optimism in the PT campaign following improved polling numbers in recent weeks.
